I've spent a good while actually living in it, not just glancing — signed in, saved a fresh link, renamed one that was already sitting there without re-pasting anything, deleted one for good, dropped things into Read later and pulled them back out, and leaned on search hard. And it holds up beautifully:

- Pasting the Rome link again with a pile of newsletter "utm" tracking junk on the end didn't spawn a copy — it recognized my existing bookmark, exactly the clutter-avoidance I cared about.
- Search does everything we settled: a plain "ROME" in capitals still finds matches across titles, notes, and addresses; `tag:articles` targets the actual label rather than the stray word; "walking guide" in quotes pins the exact phrase; and combining with AND / NOT to exclude a tag behaves just as we agreed.
- Saving a page that couldn't be reached still let me keep it with my own title, and my title stayed mine.
- The saved copy is really there — it held onto who wrote it and when it was published, so the content survives even if the page doesn't.
- Editing anytime and permanent delete — the two things I asked to add — both work cleanly.

This is the organized, searchable, trustworthy personal library I set out wanting, turning my scattered links into something I can actually rely on. I'm happy with it and I accept it.

The handful of polish items we set aside — how it feels on my phone, very long articles, a big library, and keeping the tag entry uncluttered as my tags pile up — I'm content to leave for the next round; they don't hold up my acceptance today.

Thank you — this is exactly what I hoped for.
